wa_black_wall.blurb: Black Wall is a small cliff on Mt. Erie near Anacortes, in the Orange Area of the San Juan and Fidalgo region. Despite the name, most of it is slab, with a few steeper sections. Ten routes, almost all of them trad and one sport, run from about 5.5 up to 5.9, so it suits moderate climbers who place their own gear. Protection is a blend of natural gear and bolts, and some climbs feel adventurous. The dark streaks drain through winter and spring, and parts of the rock carry lichen and moss, though there are some clean stretches too. Approach along the Cedar Trail.

wa_squirrelhouse_rock.blurb: Squirrelhouse Rock is a sport crag at Mazama in the Methow Valley, one of the Phun Rock walls and the nearest to the parking lot, just visible through the trees. A gully-like niche splits the face, and routes climb inside it and on either side. All ten routes are bolted, with grades spread from the mid 5.6 range through the 5.9s and 5.10s to a few 5.12s. The wall is in shade all day, which helps on hot afternoons. Good for a mixed group wanting some moderates alongside harder lines.
wa_squirrelhouse_rock.parking_note: Leave the car in the lot on Lost River Road, a little over a mile west of the Mazama Store; the wall is a short walk from there.

wa_2_middle_earth.blurb: Middle Earth is the first section of the Ozone cliff band on the Washington side of the Columbia Gorge, reached first on the usual approach. Where the trail forks, the left branch climbs to a bulge of rock and the routes off it make up this sector. Ten climbs, half sport and half trad, run from easy 5.6 up to 5.11, with most falling between 5.8 and 5.10. It is known for good warm-up routes, plus a few cracks for those carrying gear. Ozone overall has plenty of shaded walls and draws crowds on dry days and weekends.
